We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 135.80, 117.40, 70.50, 54.00, 43.70 ppm. Need to determine number of CH3 groups in the compound. Use carbon shifts to infer functional groups. Typically methyl carbon appears around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but here we have 43.70 and 54.00 maybe for methyl attached to heteroatoms (e.g., O-CH3 ~55 ppm, N-CH3 ~40-45). Also 70.5 could be a carbon attached to O (like CH2-O). 135.8 and 117.4 are aromatic/sp2 carbons.

Thus likely molecule has maybe one O-CH3 (methoxy) and maybe one N-CH3? But we have only two upfield signals: 43.70 and 54.00. Both could be methyls. Could be two methyl groups. Need to decide number of CH3 groups.

We could also get proton NMR to confirm. Let's request proton NMR.
